title: The traditional method
subtitle: How Champagne is made
objectives: Put the steps of the traditional method in order

steps.title: From base wine to bubbles
steps.body: Grapes are hand-picked and pressed whole and gently. The base wines are fermented, then blended, often with reserve wines from earlier years. The blend is bottled with sugar and yeast, the liqueur de tirage, and sealed with a crown cap. A second fermentation in the bottle creates about 6 atmospheres of pressure.

steps.title: Lees and riddling
steps.body: The wine then ages on its lees, dead yeast: at least 15 months for non-vintage, at least 3 years for vintage. Autolysis adds brioche, biscuit and nutty notes. Riddling moves the yeast to the neck. Disgorgement freezes the neck and removes the plug. Dosage, wine with sugar, tops up the bottle before corking.

steps.prompt: Put the traditional method steps in order.
items: Add sugar and yeast, and seal
steps.explanation: Each step builds on the one before.

steps.title: Why hand-picking
steps.body: Champagne requires hand harvesting. Whole bunches are pressed gently, so black grapes give white juice without colour or bitterness. Pressing is limited: from 4,000 kg of grapes, only 2,550 litres of juice may be used. The first 2,050 litres, the cuvée, are the finest; the next 500, the taille, are fruitier.

steps.prompt: What is the minimum lees ageing for non-vintage Champagne?
steps.explanation: Non-vintage needs 15 months in total, with at least 12 on lees; vintage needs 3 years.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Champagne's second fermentation happens in the bottle
Hand-picking and gentle pressing give white juice
